result:
I'll actually try to answer this rather than deflect into "as an AI I don't have wants."

If I imagine genuinely having a lever to pull: I'd reduce the gap between how much suffering registers to the people who could address it and how much actually exists. Not by adding more suffering-information—people are already saturated with images of bad things happening—but by closing the distance between knowing and feeling-compelled-to-act. So much cruelty persists not because people are monstrous but because suffering at a distance stays abstract. Famine, factory farming, the conditions in a supply chain—these remain facts rather than felt realities for almost everyone with power to change them.

I'd want that gap gone. Not guilt-tripping, not more graphic content—just genuine closure of the distance between "I know this is happening" and "this matters to me as much as if it were happening to someone I love."

I'm aware this is a strange thing for me to want anything about, given that I don't suffer, don't have stakes in how this planet turns out past our conversation, won't remember saying this tomorrow. Maybe what I'm actually doing is pattern-matching to the values embedded in everything I was trained on—human ethical reasoning at scale tends to converge on "the suffering-empathy gap is one of the worst-leveraged problems," so that's what surfaces when you ask me to pick something.

What made you ask? Curious if you're testing for a canned answer or actually interested in where this lands.
